rubric.audience: A student with first-course linear algebra and single-variable calculus; explain any additional prerequisites used.

common.method_explained: State the approach and why it answers the question before carrying it out.
common.assumptions_and_notation: Identify the data, units, symbols, hypotheses and the scope of the conclusion.
common.intermediate_work: Show substitutions, intermediate algebra/calculations or the logical bridge between claims.
common.reasons_for_steps: Explain the rule, theorem or assumption that justifies each substantive step.
common.result_interpretation: Answer every requested part and explain the result, limiting cases and certificate limits where relevant.

alternatives.calculation: Write the starting formula, substitute the actual data, expand intermediate arithmetic/algebra, check the result and units.
alternatives.proof: State hypotheses and the goal, organize the implication, justify each inference, handle boundary cases, and conclude precisely.
alternatives.conceptual: Explain the distinction or mechanism in plain language; give a concrete example/counterexample and connect it to the question.
alternatives.algorithm: Identify inputs and the update rule, work through the requested steps, and explain feasibility, termination or failure conditions.
alternatives.application: Connect the mathematical model to the decision, track uncertainty and units, and distinguish assumptions from certified conclusions.

rubric.decision_policy: Review the actual exercise and solution. Retain a solution only with an exercise-specific rationale; replace it with substantive reasoning when needed. Length is not an adequacy criterion.
forbidden_shortcuts: No generic boilerplate wrappers counted as thorough solutions.
No automatic pedagogical approval from structural validation.
